column1: # dcgm-exporter counter list for cawl-inferior's RTX 3090.
# ANSIBLE-MANAGED. Copied verbatim (ansible.builtin.copy
# playbooks/ai-hosts.yml under the `metrics` tag
# AI_METRICS_COMPOSE_SERVICE_FILES in the Internal group_vars/ai_hosts/
# config-metrics.yml
# read-only into the container at /etc/dcgm-exporter/custom-counters.csv. The
# exporter is pointed at it with --collectors; editing this file re-copies it
# AND restarts ai-metrics in the same run. Edit here
# FORMAT
# columns — DCGM field name
# with '#' is a comment. The field name is also the emitted metric name
# rename here is a dashboard-breaking change.
# WHY A CUSTOM LIST AT ALL. The shipped default is wrong for this host in both
# directions. It ENABLES five DCGM_FI_PROF_* profiling fields
# GPM/profiling context on the card and are documented by the image as requiring
# CAP_SYS_ADMIN; on a single-GPU box whose whole purpose is serving a model to
# 24 GB of VRAM that is not a metric
column2: it is a tenant. And it OMITS framebuffer

column1: # total
column3: the enforced power limit and the clock-event bitmask

column1: # are four of the things the dashboard exists to show.
# THE HARD RULE: ZERO DCGM_FI_PROF_* ENTRIES. Not commented-out-but-tempting
# not "just GR_ENGINE_ACTIVE". Every field below is a plain NVML read through
# the embedded host engine
column2: costs no GPU context and allocates no framebuffer.

column1: # `nvidia-smi` showing no dcgm-exporter process holding memory is the acceptance
# test for that claim
# FIELD-NAME SPELLINGS. go-dcgm v1.4601.1 renamed a number of these
# (GPU_TEMP -> GPU_TEMP_CELSIUS
# CLOCK_THROTTLE_REASONS -> CLOCKS_EVENT_REASONS
# keeps the old names resolvable through a legacy map the exporter consults
# (dcgm.IsLegacyField). The spellings used below are the ones the pinned image's
# own default-counters.csv uses
column2: which is also what every published DCGM

column1: # dashboard queries. Move to the new names only together with the dashboard.
# NOT INCLUDED
#   * DCGM_FI_DRIVER_VERSION and the other `label`-type fields. A label field
#     attaches itself to EVERY series this exporter emits
#     would break series continuity across the whole GPU dashboard to record a
#     string that is already in the change log.
#   * ECC
column3: row-remap and NVLink counters. The 3090 has no ECC and

column1: #     no NVLink peer; every one of them would be a constant zero.
#   * DCGM_EXP_CLOCK_EVENTS_COUNT / DCGM_EXP_XID_ERRORS_COUNT. Both are
#     windowed re-derivations of data already below
column2: and the window is a flag

column1: #     (--clock-events-count-window-size / --xid-count-window-size) that has to
#     agree with the scrape interval to mean anything.
# Utilization. Sample period is product-dependent; on this card both are NVML's
# coarse 1-second averages
column2: which is why they can read 0 during a short burst

column1: # and why the dashboard must not treat them as duty cycle.
DCGM_FI_DEV_GPU_UTIL
DCGM_FI_DEV_MEM_COPY_UTIL
# Framebuffer. TOTAL is the field the shipped default omits and without which
# "VRAM used" has no denominator. RESERVED is included so the three add up:
# used + free + reserved = total
column2: and a dashboard that plots used against total

column1: # alone silently loses the several hundred MiB the driver holds back.
DCGM_FI_DEV_FB_TOTAL
DCGM_FI_DEV_FB_USED
DCGM_FI_DEV_FB_FREE
DCGM_FI_DEV_FB_RESERVED
column3: Framebuffer memory reserved by the driver (in MiB).

column1: # Temperature. Core and memory only. Hotspot/junction is not exposed by NVML on
# GeForce parts at all
column2: so it is not obtainable here by any DCGM field —

column1: # CoolerControl on this host reads it out of band and remains the only source.
# MEMORY_TEMP may itself report unsupported on this card; the dashboard treats a
# missing series as absent data
DCGM_FI_DEV_GPU_TEMP
DCGM_FI_DEV_MEMORY_TEMP
# Power. Draw and the limit it is being held against
# on its own cannot distinguish an idle card from a power-capped one.
DCGM_FI_DEV_POWER_USAGE
DCGM_FI_DEV_ENFORCED_POWER_LIMIT
# Fan. Percent of maximum
column2: not RPM: NVML reports the card's fan as a duty cycle.

DCGM_FI_DEV_SM_CLOCK
DCGM_FI_DEV_MEM_CLOCK
